title: Preserve pet-type integrity for customer-service writes
problem: A pet create or update request can name a pet-type identifier that the service cannot resolve. The write must not leave or persist a pet with incomplete type information.
context: This is a learner-local TRAINING exercise against the selected PetClinic revision, not an upstream issue or contribution request.
impact: Invalid relationships should fail predictably without persisting incomplete domain state.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: An unknown pet-type identifier is rejected and no incomplete pet is persisted.
Existing valid create and update behavior remains supported.
Focused automated tests cover the invalid and valid paths and pass at the submitted revision.
The learner explains the chosen failure contract, one rejected alternative, and the first likely failure case.

constraints: Do not change database schemas, service boundaries, or remote infrastructure.
Do not push or open an upstream pull request as part of this task.

scope.description: One domain-write boundary and its focused tests.

investigation_areas: Pet creation and update request path
Existing customer-service web and repository tests
testing_expectations: Run ./mvnw -pl spring-petclinic-customers-service test from the repository root.
investigation_prompt: Trace the pet create/update path and predict what happens when the requested pet type cannot be resolved. Do not change code until your design is reviewed.
documentation_requirements: Record the failure contract, rejected alternative, and first likely failure case in the learner design.

next_task_preview.title: Trace the pet-write failure contract through the API gateway
next_task_preview.summary: Map how the customer-service error is represented at the gateway boundary and propose a focused compatibility check without changing TASK-001.
